content.text:
**The core prototype was working by 5 October, but a fully verified assignment-complete claim is still unsupported.**

1. **Private collection, resumption and reuse: demonstrated historically.** Real Slack + controlled-site runs privately collected a password/code, automatically resumed, reused the saved password in a fresh browser, and kept values out of Slack/model transcripts. [Hosted-vault evidence](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/evidence/2026-10-05-hosted-vault.md:14). Transient browser failures also recovered without controller intervention at lines 34–37. This proves the older local POC, not the subsequently replaced Managed Auth implementation.

2. **Automatic TOTP: implemented, still missing decisive live acceptance.** The current owner-only dashboard accepts an authenticator setup key, forwards it to Kernel, and never returns the seed/code to the agent: [implementation](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/managed_auth.py:192), [provider boundary](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/cloud_browser/kernel_auth_client.py:400). On 11 October at 17:15 IST, fresh provider login and GitHub repository followups succeeded autonomously, but the ledger explicitly records `totp_autonomous_verified: false`. The later 19:49 run also did not reach a challenge. [Current ledger](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/clanker-qa/batches/2026-10-11-reliability-round6/CAMPAIGN.json:331). **This is the clearest remaining core requirement gap.**

3. **Revocation: substantial implementation and controlled evidence.** The October 6 real Chromium probe exercised owner/recipient separation, invited login, revoked-grant refusal, recipient cookie-profile removal and owner-browser preservation. [Evidence](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/decisions/2026-10-06-vault-invitations.md:142). Current Kernel revocation blocks subsequent use until remote cleanup is confirmed; browser deletion does not revoke the merchant account itself. [Current documented boundary](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/ACCESS_MANAGEMENT.md:114). Current persistent-principal revocation tests use fixture Kernel/CDP I/O, so do not describe those as fresh live acceptance. [Integration evidence](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/decisions/2026-10-11-persistent-browser-integration.md:55).

4. **Background browser work and recovery: clearly beyond a bare scaffold.** Current live GitHub work succeeded with no human sign-in intervention. Earlier live Kernel/Slack shopping prepared a verified cart; later benchmark records provide broader successes. Durable recovery was activated and delivered exactly one automatic continuation into the original isolated flight task, though that evidence did not prove booking completion. [Recovery evidence](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/evidence/2026-10-08-task-continuation-recovery.md:19).

5. **Submission is distinct from building the prototype.** The submission checklist still calls for clean-machine setup verification, reviewer deployed access, an approximately two-minute real demo, and final isolation/TOTP checks; publication/reviewer contact are pending owner review. [Checklist](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/SUBMISSION.md:7). Avoid citing the README’s stale 0/12 figure or treating the expanded benchmark as the assignment’s own mandatory scope.

**Useful framing:** “You had a working core prototype around 5–6 October. Since then you’ve expanded it into a larger product and reliability project. Some later work is optional expansion, but automatic TOTP proof, access isolation/revocation confidence and final submission packaging are still completion work.”
